instruments.title: The International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019
applies_to: Financial products, financial services and financial institutions in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), including GIFT IFSC
key_concepts: Financial institution, financial product, financial service and IFSC (s. 3)
Duty to develop and regulate financial products, services and institutions in the IFSC (s. 12)
Powers of RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA under the First Schedule Acts exercised by IFSCA in the IFSC (s. 13)
Transactions in the foreign currency the Authority specifies (s. 20)
core_obligations: s. 13(1): in an IFSC, the powers of the appropriate regulators under the First Schedule Acts (including the RBI Act, Banking Regulation Act, FEMA, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, SEBI Act, Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, Depositories Act, Insurance Act, IRDA Act and PFRDA Act) are exercised by IFSCA alone, so far as they relate to regulating financial products, services and institutions
s. 13(4): the provisions of those Acts on registration, reports, inspection, investigation, adjudication, compounding, appeals and penalties apply to IFSC entities as they apply under those Acts
s. 20: transactions of financial services in an IFSC are carried on in the foreign currency the Authority specifies, in consultation with the Central Government
s. 30: the Act has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law
consequences_stated: s. 13(5): penalties, fines, fees and settlement amounts are collected in the foreign currency equivalent, at the RBI reference rate on the date of the order
instruments.consequences_general: International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019: in an IFSC, IFSCA exercises all the powers of RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA under the Acts listed in the First Schedule (s. 13(1)). The provisions of those Acts on inspection, investigation, prosecution, settlement, compounding, adjudication, appeals, and the fees, fines and penalties for contravention apply to IFSC products, services and institutions as they apply under those Acts (s. 13(4)). Penalties, fines, fees and settlement amounts are collected in the foreign currency equivalent, at the RBI rate on the date of the order (s. 13(5)). Each IFSCA regulation also lets the Authority suspend, withdraw or cancel a registration, licence or recognition after giving the entity an opportunity to make its submissions.

applies_to: IFSC units that hold an SNRR account with an AD bank in India under the Foreign Exchange Management (Deposit) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations, 2025
key_concepts: SNRR account with an AD bank outside the IFSC for business outside the IFSC
Transfer of rupee receipts to the unit's IBU account in foreign currency

instruments.title: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Banking) Regulations, 2020 (consolidated, with the 2024 amendment)
applies_to: IFSC Banking Units: an IFSC Banking Unit set up as a branch (IBU) or an IFSC Banking Company set up as a subsidiary (IBC)
Representative offices and Global Administrative Offices of banks in the IFSC
key_concepts: Banking Unit as IBU (branch) or IBC (subsidiary)
LCR, NSFR, leverage and exposure norms
No cash; savings accounts only for individuals
core_obligations: reg 3(3): an IBU keeps minimum capital of USD 20 million (maintained at the parent bank), with a no-objection from the home regulator and a liquidity support undertaking
reg 3(3A): an IBC keeps minimum capital of USD 50 million
reg 4: an IBU also follows its home regulator's directions
reg 5: a Banking Unit maintains the LCR (an IBU may, with approval, hold it at the parent) and the NSFR as the Authority specifies
regs 6 and 7: leverage ratio and exposure norms as specified
reg 8: no CRR on deposits generally, but deposits from individuals attract reserve ratios as specified; an IBC keeps reserves as the Banking Regulation Act and RBI Act require
reg 9: no lender-of-last-resort support is available to a Banking Unit

reg 10: business is conducted in the specified foreign currencies (First Schedule: USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, AUD, CHF, HKD, SGD, AED, RUB, and since 2024 SEK, NOK, NZD and DKK); rupee transactions are settled in a specified currency
reg 11: foreign currency accounts may be opened for residents within the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
reg 12: no cash transactions; savings accounts only for individuals
reg 13: activities permitted under IFSCA Act s. 3(1)(e) and Banking Regulation Act s. 6 unless prohibited; referral services allowed
reg 14: follow the IFSCA AML, CFT and KYC guidelines
regs 15 to 17: report in USD, keep books in the specified currencies, and keep a rupee account only for administrative expenses
reg 19: netting of margins as specified
consequences_stated: reg 21: the Authority may withdraw the licence or permission after giving the Banking Unit 30 days to make its submissions

instruments.title: IFSCA Banking Handbook: General (GEN v5.0), Conduct of Business (COB v6.0) and Prudential (PRU v5.0) Directions
applies_to: IBUs and IBCs in the IFSC
key_concepts: Credit risk policy and large exposures
core_obligations: PRU: an IBU keeps base capital of USD 20 million; its leverage ratio is maintained by the parent as the home regulator requires
PRU: maintain an LCR of 100% (from 01-04-2021) or the home regulator's minimum where that is higher
PRU: a currency is significant where it is more than 10% of liabilities (or a lower home threshold), and LCR is tracked for it
PRU: keep a funding strategy reviewed at least every three years, a board-approved credit risk policy and large exposure limits
COB: conduct-of-business rules for customer dealings, including Module 16 on providing credit
timelines: PRU: file the quarterly capital adequacy and leverage certificate within 45 days of the end of each quarter

instruments.title: Amendments to Module 16 (Providing Credit) of the IFSCA Banking Handbook: COB Directions

key_concepts: Banking Regulation Act s. 20(1) disapplied for foreign bank IBUs

instruments.title: Internet banking services to clients of IBUs: Review (29-12-2025, as amended 30-06-2026 and 31-07-2026)
applies_to: IBUs offering liability products (deposits and accounts) to customers
excluded: IBUs without liability products are exempt from the interactive and transactional requirements
key_concepts: Unified dashboard for all linked accounts (deposit and loan)
Dual-layer authentication, maker-checker and beneficiary whitelisting
Bar on onboarding new customers if non-compliant
core_obligations: Offer internet banking with explicit customer consent, and display the specified currencies and cut-off times

Provide a unified dashboard with real-time balances of all linked accounts (deposit and loan), machine-readable statements, inward remittance instructions, premature withdrawal and SMS or email alerts (live rates are not mandatory)

timelines: Original deadline 31-07-2026, extended once to 30-09-2026
consequences_stated: From 01-10-2026, an IBU that has not complied stops onboarding new customers for the liability product concerned

instruments.title: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021 (as amended up to 07-05-2026)
instruments.theme: Finance companies, leasing and treasury centres
applies_to: Finance Companies (subsidiary, joint venture or new company in the IFSC) and Finance Units (branch of an entity incorporated in India or abroad)
key_concepts: Core activities (lending, factoring and forfaiting, investments, derivatives, treasury centres)
Non-core activities (merchant banking, advisory, operating leases, distribution and others)
Capital ratio, LCR and exposure ceiling
core_obligations: reg 3: no Finance Company or Finance Unit carries on business without a certificate of registration; a regulated parent needs a home regulator no-objection; the applicant comes from a FATF-compliant jurisdiction

reg 3: a Finance Unit may undertake core activities only if it is a regulated financial institution with a no-objection, except a treasury centre; an LLP or trust may undertake non-core activities only

reg 4: an entity doing core activities keeps a capital ratio of 8% of risk-weighted assets, keeps an LCR (a Finance Unit may hold it at the parent with approval), and does not exceed 25% of its eligible capital base to a single counterparty or group without approval

reg 5: core activities are lending (loans, guarantees, credit enhancement, securitisation, financial lease, portfolio buys and sales), factoring and forfaiting, investments, derivatives and global or regional corporate treasury centres; non-core activities include merchant banking, investment advisory, portfolio management, operating leases of aircraft, ships and equipment, distribution and similar services

reg 5: non-core activities sit in a separately identifiable department with firewalls; entities doing only non-core activities use derivatives only to hedge; no speculative transactions; dealings with residents are subject to FEMA
reg 6: deal in freely convertible foreign currency, keep a rupee account only for administrative expenses, and keep the balance sheet in USD
reg 7: follow the KYC and AML requirements that apply to Banking Units
reg 8: follow the governance guidelines; prior approval for any change in control (20% or more)
reg 9: report to the Authority in USD
timelines: reg 3: an applicant has 30 days to rectify deficiencies the Authority points out
reg 8: a Finance Unit intimates a change in control of its parent within 15 days
consequences_stated: reg 11: on failure to meet a registration condition, the Authority may suspend, withdraw or cancel the registration after giving the entity an opportunity to make its submissions

instruments.title: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 10-09-2026)
applies_to: Fund Management Entities (FMEs) in the IFSC and the schemes they manage: venture capital, restricted and retail schemes, portfolio management, investment trusts and family investment funds
key_concepts: Authorised FME, Registered FME (Non-Retail) and Registered FME (Retail)
Principal officer, compliance officer and KMPs based in the IFSC
Scheme corpus, minimum investment and manager contribution
core_obligations: reg 3: register as an Authorised FME (venture capital schemes, family investment funds), a Registered FME (Non-Retail) (restricted schemes, portfolio management, private investment trusts) or a Registered FME (Retail) (retail schemes, public investment trusts, ETFs)
reg 5: the FME is a company, LLP or branch
reg 7: appoint a principal officer; a Registered FME also appoints a compliance officer; KMPs are based in the IFSC and complete the specified certification
reg 8 and Second Schedule: net worth of USD 75,000 (Authorised), USD 500,000 (Non-Retail) or USD 1,000,000 (Retail); a branch may hold it at the parent
Venture capital scheme: corpus USD 3 million to USD 200 million; minimum investment USD 250,000 (unless accredited); manager contribution at least 2.5% of corpus or USD 750,000, whichever is lower

Restricted scheme: minimum investment USD 150,000 (unless accredited); corpus USD 3 million; manager contribution 2.5% or USD 750,000 (close-ended) and 5% or USD 1.5 million (open-ended), whichever is lower
Retail scheme: at least 20 investors and corpus USD 3 million; minimum USD 10,000 where more than 15% is in unlisted securities
Portfolio management minimum USD 75,000 per client; family investment fund minimum corpus USD 10 million
reg 118: follow the Code of Conduct in the Third Schedule; reg 124: no guaranteed returns
regs 121 and 122: keep a business continuity plan reviewed every year and a cyber security framework
reg 132: appoint an independent custodian where required, including for schemes with AUM above USD 70 million
timelines: reg 7: a Retail FME appoints a fund-management KMP before its first retail scheme; an FME whose AUM reaches USD 1 billion appoints an additional KMP within 6 months
Restricted scheme may start investing after USD 1 million and reach USD 3 million within 12 months
reg 119: keep records for 8 years, and scheme records for 5 years after winding up
consequences_stated: reg 143: the Authority may suspend or cancel the registration

instruments.consequences_general: International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019: in an IFSC, IFSCA exercises all the powers of RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA under the Acts listed in the First Schedule (s. 13(1)). The provisions of those Acts on inspection, investigation, prosecution, settlement, compounding, adjudication, appeals, and the fees, fines and penalties for contravention apply to IFSC products, services and institutions as they apply under those Acts (s. 13(4)). Penalties, fines, fees and settlement amounts are collected in the foreign currency equivalent, at the RBI rate on the date of the order (s. 13(5)). Each IFSCA regulation also lets the Authority suspend, withdraw or cancel a registration, licence or recognition after giving the entity an opportunity to make its submissions.

instruments.short_name: Cyber security and cyber resilience guidelines
instruments.title: Guidelines on Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience for regulated entities in IFSCs (10-03-2025, as amended 10-03-2026)
instruments.theme: Fees, SEZ approval and cyber security
applies_to: All regulated entities in the IFSC
excluded: For three years from 10-03-2026: branches of regulated entities, group-only entities such as global in-house centres and entities with fewer than 10 employees adopt the parent's framework and file a certificate instead
key_concepts: Annual cyber audit by a CERT-In empanelled auditor
core_obligations: Appoint a CISO or designated officer; the governing board and senior management oversee cyber security
Have an annual cyber audit by a CERT-In empanelled or certified auditor
Exempt entities adopt the parent framework (the parent CISO acts as designated officer), file a compliance certificate and still submit the annual audit
timelines: Report cyber incidents to cyber-incidents@ifsca.gov.in within 6 hours of detection
Submit the audit report within 90 days of the end of the financial year (or within 7 days of filing with a market infrastructure institution)

instruments.title: Fee structure for entities undertaking or intending to undertake permissible activities in IFSC (02-03-2026, with corrigendum of 13-03-2026)
instruments.theme: Fees, SEZ approval and cyber security
applies_to: All applicants and regulated entities in the IFSC
key_concepts: Application, registration, flat recurring and conditional recurring fees
core_obligations: Pay the application and registration fees for each activity, the flat recurring fee each year and any conditional recurring fee
Late payment attracts interest
timelines: The flat recurring fee falls due on 1 April and is paid by 30 April
New registrants pay a pro-rata fee within 15 days of the grant
Conditional fee true-up by 30 April of the next financial year
